name: Pano
author: support@panomc.com
description: Pano is an open-source web platform for Minecraft servers: website, web store and management panel in one. Create a database for the server (Databases tab) and fill the database variables, or enter it in the setup wizard. https://panomc.com

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Pano egg install script (Pterodactyl / Pelican). Runs as root in ghcr.io/pterodactyl/installers:debian
# with the server's files at /mnt/server, on install and on every reinstall. It downloads the Pano jar
# (PANO_VERSION, or the newest of PANO_CHANNEL), checks its sha256, points .pano-jar at it and writes
# start.sh. Data (config.conf, plugins, themes, uploads) is never touched, so a reinstall is an upgrade.
#
# build-egg.sh embeds start.sh at the __START_SH__ line below; edit start.sh, not the egg.
set -euo pipefail

API_URL=${PANO_API_URL:-https://api.panomc.com}
VERSION=${PANO_VERSION:-latest}
CHANNEL=${PANO_CHANNEL:-release}
[ "$VERSION" = latest ] && VERSION=

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server

json_field() { sed -n "s/.*\"$1\":\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p"; }

# The release list answers {"data":{"release":[...],"beta":[...],"alpha":[...]}}, newest first.
# One release object per line, keeping the channel it came from in front of it.
releases=$(curl -fsSL "$API_URL/releases/platform" | sed 's/"\(release\|beta\|alpha\)":\[/\n@\1\n/g' | tr '{' '\n' |
  awk '/^@/ { channel = substr($0, 2); next } /"releaseTag"/ { print channel " " $0 }') || releases=

if [ -n "$VERSION" ]; then
  line=$(printf '%s\n' "$releases" | grep -F "\"releaseTag\":\"v${VERSION#v}\"" | head -n 1 || true)
else
  line=$(printf '%s\n' "$releases" | grep "^$CHANNEL " | head -n 1 || true)
fi

if [ -n "$line" ]; then
  tag=$(printf '%s' "$line" | json_field releaseTag)
  url=$(printf '%s' "$line" | json_field downloadUrl)
  hash=$(printf '%s' "$line" | json_field hash)
  hash=${hash#sha256:}
elif [ -n "$VERSION" ]; then
  # older than what the list holds: straight from the GitHub release
  tag="v${VERSION#v}"
  url="https://github.com/PanoMC/Pano/releases/download/$tag/Pano-${tag#v}.jar"
  hash=$(curl -fsSL "$url.sha256" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1 || true)
else
  echo "No Pano release found in the $CHANNEL channel ($API_URL/releases/platform)." >&2
  exit 1
fi

jar="Pano-${tag#v}.jar"
current=$(cat .pano-jar 2>/dev/null || true)

if [ -f "$jar" ] && [ -n "$hash" ] && [ "$(sha256sum "$jar" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$hash" ]; then
  echo "Pano ${tag#v} is already installed."
else
  echo "Downloading Pano ${tag#v}..."
  curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$jar.part" "$url"
  if [ -n "$hash" ]; then
    actual=$(sha256sum "$jar.part" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    if [ "$actual" != "$hash" ]; then
      rm -f "$jar.part"
      echo "Checksum mismatch for $jar: expected $hash, got $actual" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
  mv -f "$jar.part" "$jar"
fi

# Same layout as Pano's JarPointer: .pano-jar names the jar, .pano-jar.previous the one before it.
if [ -n "$current" ] && [ "$current" != "$jar" ] && [ -f "$current" ]; then
  printf '%s' "$current" >.pano-jar.previous
fi
printf '%s' "$jar" >.pano-jar
for old in Pano-*.jar; do
  [ "$old" = "$jar" ] || [ "$old" = "$(cat .pano-jar.previous 2>/dev/null || true)" ] || rm -f "$old"
done

cat >start.sh <<'PANO_START_SH'
#!/bin/bash
# Pano launcher for Pterodactyl / Pelican (the egg's startup command runs it from /home/container).
# Same semantics as docker/runtime/pano-launcher.sh: the jar is named by .pano-jar (re-read on every
# start, which also puts Pano in container mode), stdin is kept for the console, SIGTERM/SIGINT are
# forwarded and the child's exit code is returned, exit 75 = planned restart / self-update -> relaunch
# in place. Pterodactyl itself would treat exit 75 as a stop.
set -f
cd /home/container || exit 1
exec 3<&0

data=$PWD
port=${SERVER_PORT:-8088}
jvm_args=${PANO_JVM_ARGS:-"-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=${JAVA_RAM_PERCENT:-60}"}

# Pano reads PANO_HTTP_PORT only when it creates config.conf; after that the allocation can still change.
export PANO_HTTP_PORT=$port
if [ -f "$data/config.conf" ]; then
  sed -i "s/^\([[:space:]]*\)http-port[[:space:]]*=.*/\1http-port=$port/" "$data/config.conf"
fi

# jansi / jline unpack their natives next to the app instead of /tmp
natives="$data/.cache/natives"

stop=0
pid=
trap 'stop=1; [ -n "$pid" ] && kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null' TERM INT

while :; do
  # a stop that lands between a planned exit and the relaunch ends the server
  [ "$stop" = 1 ] && exit 0
  jar=$(cat "$data/.pano-jar" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$jar" in
    ''|*/*|.|..) jar= ;;
  esac
  if [ -z "$jar" ] || [ ! -f "$data/$jar" ]; then
    echo "pano: .pano-jar does not name a jar, reinstall the server" >&2
    exit 64
  fi
  mkdir -p "$natives" 2>/dev/null || true
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # PANO_JVM_ARGS is a space separated list, globbing is off (set -f)
  java "-Duser.home=$data" "-Djansi.tmpdir=$natives" "-Djline.tmpdir=$natives" $jvm_args -jar "$data/$jar" -nogui <&3 &
  pid=$!
  wait "$pid"; code=$?
  while [ "$stop" = 1 ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do wait "$pid"; code=$?; done
  [ "$stop" = 1 ] && exit "$code"
  [ "$code" = 75 ] || exit "$code"
  pid=
  echo "pano: planned restart (exit 75)" >&2
done
PANO_START_SH
chmod 0755 start.sh

echo "Pano ${tag#v} installed. Start the server, then open its address to finish the setup wizard."

variables.name: Pano version
variables.description: A version such as 1.1.0, or latest for the newest release of the channel below. Reinstall the server to apply; Pano can also update itself from its panel.

variables.name: Release channel
variables.description: Channel that latest installs from: release, beta or alpha.

variables.name: Java memory (%)
variables.description: Share of the server memory the JVM may use. The rest is left to the website processes Pano runs next to it (about 200 MB each).

variables.name: Database host
variables.description: MariaDB / MySQL host. Read on the first start only; leave empty to enter the database in the setup wizard.
